reviewKind: test-backed behavior and migration guidance, not blanket backwards-compatibility guarantee

entries.behavior: Scope cancellation, closed-scope admission and child cleanup
entries.migration: Existing scope entry points remain available; validate closed scope rejection and exactly-once child cancellation before replacing caller-owned cancellation.

entries.behavior: Future state, awaited result and cancellation-aware cleanup
entries.migration: Future await and callback completion preserve existing exception propagation; annotations document the contract without runtime changes.

entries.behavior: Cancellation/deadline timer suspension and idempotent wait cleanup
entries.migration: Nullable unlimited deadlines do not schedule timers; non-null finite deadlines continue to follow the same cancellation and wakeup order.

entries.behavior: Bounded coroutine ready-depth high-water measurement, task lifecycle, and FIFO resume fairness
entries.migration: The internal scheduler retains the same bounded ready queue and diagnostic high-water metric; verify FIFO resume, cancellation and task cleanup after inline sampling. Internal implementation changes do not introduce new caller migration requirements.

entries.behavior: Future readiness and failed-child propagation
entries.migration: Preserve observed resolve/reject callback ordering when upgrading; avoid treating a settled future as a resumable scheduling slot.

entries.behavior: One-time suspension arming, future resolution and cancellation
entries.migration: Continue using futures through CoroutineScope; completion and cancellation must still settle an awaiting task exactly once.

entries.behavior: Event-loop suspension and cancellation cleanup
entries.migration: Awaited loop callbacks must continue to resume the correct task without leaking a watcher or resuming a cancelled waiter.

entries.behavior: Asynchronous socket coroutine completion and ownership
entries.migration: Migrate to worker-owned async connections with cancellation propagation; do not reuse connection ownership after a scope ends.

entries.behavior: Task Fiber lifetime and scheduler-owned completion
entries.migration: Psalm Fiber generic annotation follows the current toolchain without changing the task execution or cancellation contract.

entries.behavior: HTTP/1 response lifecycle and flushing semantics
entries.migration: Response writers continue enforcing start, write, terminal completion and backpressure behavior across HTTP/1 requests.

entries.behavior: HTTP/1 request-line, header and connection framing validation
entries.migration: Preserve bounds on HTTP/1 request headers, parsing and smuggling protections; no endpoint should bypass existing validation or framing checks.

entries.behavior: H2 stream admission, flow control and graceful GOAWAY
entries.migration: Keep accepted streams draining after GOAWAY; new H2 limits may reject invalid peer streams that older handlers tolerated.

entries.behavior: HTTP/2 header and body completion semantics
entries.migration: Preserve HTTP/2 response suppression, content-length rules, finalization and flow-control handling at the writer boundary.

entries.behavior: Bounded H2 peer control-frame state
entries.migration: Do not depend on unlimited SETTINGS/PING/PRIORITY floods; invalid over-budget traffic is rejected.

entries.behavior: HTTP/2 request stream admission, framing and body handler lifecycle
entries.migration: Incoming HTTP/2 stream state remains bounded, validated, and correctly reset under flow-control or handler errors; no new public stream contract is introduced.

entries.behavior: Optional DATA-credit callback for H2 outbound scheduling
entries.migration: Previously valid constructor calls retain defaults; optional outbound credit is a new capability, not a required argument.

entries.behavior: HTTP/3 final response framing and writer lifecycle
entries.migration: HTTP/3 response writers continue to finalize response streams and reject invalid transitions; QUIC capability remains optional.

entries.behavior: Adaptive HTTP/3 polling interval bounds and idle wait strategy
entries.migration: Explicit float multiplication preserves idle interval limits and effective poll behavior under backpressure without changing protocol or stream admission.

entries.behavior: HTTP/3 request stream and body admission with stream lifecycle guards
entries.migration: Keep QUIC stream state ownership, protocol validation and rejection of malformed request frames unchanged; no new stream-admission behavior is introduced.

entries.behavior: H3 stream lifetime, cancellation and QUIC state
entries.migration: Only use the H3 capability with a supported installed native QUIC extension; no WebTransport or QUIC DATAGRAM promise.

entries.behavior: Optional H3 failure observer and per-worker lifecycle
entries.migration: Existing constructor defaults remain; new connection-failure reporting is opt-in; verify sibling stream finalization.

entries.behavior: QUIC transport session ownership and native feature detection
entries.migration: Do not treat a missing native QUIC extension as a silently emulated H3 endpoint.

entries.behavior: Buffered request-body consumption and end-of-body callbacks
entries.migration: Buffered request bodies retain their bounded read and completion behavior; metadata-only method attributes do not alter payload handling.

entries.behavior: Callback writer start, data and terminal delivery
entries.migration: Callback-based response writers must preserve end-once and suppressed-body semantics without introducing new caller requirements.

entries.behavior: HTTP request header syntax, authority, content framing and protocol validation
entries.migration: Header and authority validation stays strict against request smuggling, duplicate headers and invalid pseudo-header framing; rejected requests remain rejected.

entries.behavior: Streaming request cancellation propagation and bounded body lifecycle
entries.migration: Streaming bodies continue propagating transport cancellation into request contexts; no new consumer migration is required.

entries.behavior: Monotonic time conversion bounds and nanosecond rounding
entries.migration: Explicit float conversion retains the existing finite nonnegative duration and overflow guards, preserving monotonic time semantics on supported PHP targets.

entries.behavior: ext-event scalable backend watcher registration, constant-time cancellation and timer index isolation
entries.migration: The ext-event backend maintains distinct read and write watcher slots with identical public cancellation and event callback behavior; indexed cleanup replaces linear scans without changing event registration, timer semantics or fallback selection.

entries.behavior: Host reactor callback, timer and coroutine bridge contracts
entries.migration: Swoole/OpenSwoole adapters must honor the same registered callbacks and coroutine bridge interface; native hosts remain separately validated by coroutine CI.

entries.behavior: Select fallback, callback timing, watcher cleanup
entries.migration: The SelectLoop has a bounded native connection ceiling; select timeout and errors are surfaced rather than masked.

entries.behavior: Host-owned event-loop scheduling and cancellation
entries.migration: The host-owned Swoole loop retains timer, watcher, deferred callback and coroutine progress contracts without changing caller APIs.

entries.behavior: Request ID policy with no mandated tracing-header convention
entries.migration: Request identity remains generated through the configured policy without requiring a tracing header or changing existing request metadata.

entries.behavior: Fixed-width unpredictable hexadecimal request identifiers
entries.migration: Generated IDs remain 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters and do not encode raw process IDs; no public calling convention changes.

entries.behavior: Bounded versioned runtime metric snapshots and accounting
entries.migration: Retain the versioned bounded snapshot shape and counter semantics; implementation annotation changes are metadata-only.

entries.behavior: Public onClose/write trait relocation; optional TLS identity and EOF
entries.migration: Both public methods remain available through traits; existing constructor calls retain optional defaults; strict TLS EOF must be selected explicitly.

entries.behavior: UDP datagram admission and bounded receive buffers
entries.migration: Preserve packet boundaries, peer identity and backpressure; do not interpret QUIC datagram support as WebTransport.

entries.behavior: Connection close classification and callback sequencing
entries.migration: Match explicit close reason enums rather than assuming all terminal transitions are successful EOF.

entries.behavior: Connection lifecycle state transition rules
entries.migration: Do not re-admit writes or callbacks after terminal state and worker generation changes.

entries.behavior: Bounded pending and flushed write bytes
entries.migration: Handle rejected queue submissions and partial reads without assuming unconstrained buffering.

entries.behavior: Exactly-once and same-process callback ownership
entries.migration: Do not retain asynchronous callbacks across a process fork or closed request scope.

entries.behavior: Socket option precedence and validation
entries.migration: Explicit per-connection policy may override defaults; validate host support rather than assuming all tunables exist.

entries.behavior: Nonblocking TLS readiness and verified errors
entries.migration: Trust chain, hostname/SNI, ALPN and handshake deadlines remain required; plaintext fallback after verification failure is prohibited.

entries.behavior: TCP listener process/accept ownership
entries.migration: Construct listener/accept watchers in their owning worker and enforce supervisor lifecycle boundaries.

entries.behavior: Optional client-certificate server TLS requirement
entries.migration: Existing constructor default remains; enable mTLS explicitly when a client identity is required.

entries.behavior: Unix socket ownership and cleanup
entries.migration: Delete or reuse Unix socket endpoints under ownership rules, never an unrelated host path.

entries.behavior: Length-prefixed frame validation and stream buffering
entries.migration: Keep the existing length-delimited frame encoding and buffering contract, including rejection of malformed or oversized frames.

entries.behavior: Delimited line framing with bounded decode batches
entries.migration: Framed transport consumers must retain multi-byte delimiter boundary handling and configured maximum line sizes; explicit override metadata does not change encoding.

entries.behavior: Raw TCP payloads without length-prefix buffering
entries.migration: Raw-mode users continue receiving unframed chunks without hidden buffering; the interface annotation does not change runtime payload handling.

entries.behavior: Request context activation, owned work and attribute lifecycle
entries.migration: Context lifecycle transitions, attribute validation and request identity remain unchanged; explicit exception documentation records preexisting behavior.

entries.behavior: Top-level runtime request, application lifecycle and server startup controls
entries.migration: Explicit exception contracts preserve the same startup, shutdown and runtime admission errors; no public request or runtime lifecycle signature changes.

entries.behavior: Request-bound coroutine scheduling and lifecycle ownership
entries.migration: The runtime still drains request-owned coroutine tasks before reset and completion, and propagates cancellation across each request lifetime.

entries.behavior: Hosted FPM request metadata and response contract
entries.migration: PHP-FPM continues using the host-provided request and response transport, with no newly required native event-loop or worker configuration.

entries.behavior: FrankenPHP hosted request normalization and lifecycle
entries.migration: FrankenPHP remains host-owned; maintain request-scoped state reset and HTTP response semantics without introducing native listener ownership.

entries.behavior: RoadRunner hosted request cycle and lifecycle cleanup
entries.migration: RoadRunner keeps host-owned worker process management and the shared request/response contract, including lifecycle cleanup after each request.

entries.behavior: Swoole host startup, shutdown, worker reset and response handling
entries.migration: Host-owned Swoole remains responsible for worker and coroutine lifecycle; startup, failed bootstrap and request reset semantics must not change.

entries.behavior: Host-owned request context isolation and lifecycle
entries.migration: FPM, FrankenPHP and RoadRunner own their request boundaries; avoid duplicating prefork/listener responsibilities.

entries.behavior: RoadRunner streamed response, HEAD suppression and content-length checks
entries.migration: Hosted response writers preserve frame ordering, body suppression for HEAD, and declared content-length validation after interface metadata changes.

entries.behavior: RoadRunner session request admission and response delivery
entries.migration: The request transport continues to acknowledge, respond and stop through its host-owned session contract without altering worker ownership.

entries.behavior: Persistent application lifecycle and request-scoped context cleanup
entries.migration: Application callbacks remain isolated by request contexts; completed requests cannot be re-entered, and state must be reset after each handling cycle.

entries.behavior: Conservative effective CPU and memory capacity detection across Linux cgroup quotas, malformed cpusets, and host limits
entries.migration: Valid, ordered Linux cpuset ranges retain the same host and cgroup resource semantics; malformed, duplicate or overlapping cpuset ranges now fail closed to a conservative one-CPU worker sizing value rather than incorrectly allowing full host capacity.

entries.behavior: Immutable runtime identity, capabilities and generation metadata
entries.migration: Runtime metadata remains read-only and scoped by the appropriate worker/host context; callers must not infer new capabilities from adapter annotations.

entries.behavior: Exit notification and reaped child generation
entries.migration: Never treat an exited old-generation worker as a currently accepted or ready worker.

entries.behavior: Tracked child-set ownership on scale/recycle
entries.migration: Close stale worker handles and reject duplicate slot ownership during replacement.

entries.behavior: Periodic supervisor sampling/timer cleanup
entries.migration: Stop timers on supervisor drain; do not leave periodic autoscale handles active after shutdown.

entries.behavior: Process identity transition ordering and failure handling
entries.migration: Native privilege dropping must continue validating identity and supplementary groups before irreversible GID/UID transitions, and fail closed on errors.

entries.behavior: Worker readiness signaling across fork and timeout
entries.migration: Workers only accept traffic after their own readiness handshake; stale generation readiness is invalid.

entries.behavior: Signal wake channel lifecycle, handler restoration, and cleanup
entries.migration: Closing copied resources after clearing owned properties preserves one-shot signal resource cleanup and prevents stale closed-resource references.

entries.behavior: Monotonic supervisor uptime and worker age reporting
entries.migration: Explicit float conversion keeps the same externally observable status snapshot fields and nonnegative monotonic durations.

entries.behavior: Bounded worker restart policy and exponential backoff
entries.migration: Explicit float exponentiation preserves restart retry caps, backoff ceilings and worker-failure handling.

entries.behavior: Native worker recycle, crash recovery and shutdown
entries.migration: Use explicit supervised lifecycle and drain rather than assuming Swoole/FPM host ownership; verify accepted work completes once.

entries.behavior: Per-worker admission, metrics, ownership and stop wake
entries.migration: Use the active worker context after fork; do not use a context retained from an earlier generation.

entries.behavior: Worker-group restart and capacity policy
entries.migration: Configure worker count and restart/shutdown budgets explicitly for native prefork; hosted modes remain host-owned.

entries.behavior: Optional outbound client masking expectation
entries.migration: Server parser defaults remain; explicitly enable the client-side masking contract for outbound WebSocket clients.

entries.behavior: RFC6455 server/client framing and masking
entries.migration: Honor role-specific masking and fragmentation, reject malformed payloads rather than accepting unsafe client frames.

entries.behavior: Optional outbound client-mode and close/ping lifecycle
entries.migration: Existing server mode default remains; explicitly set client role for outbound sessions and preserve close-handshake timing.
